summary: Steven Lukes works in philosophy and other fields, having studied at Balliol College and Nuffield College. His career includes posts at Balliol College (~1966–1987), the European University Institute (~1987–1995), LSE (~1995–1999), and New York University (~1999).

Steven Neal Weinberger specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his BA at Amherst College and his MA and PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and multiple traditional teachers, later holding a post there attested in 2006.

Working in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, Sthaneshwar Timalsina studied at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and the University of Halle-Wittenberg. He held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University (~1994–2004), San Diego State University (~2005–2021), and Stony Brook University (~2021).

Stig Wikander was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Uppsala and Copenhagen under Henrik Samuel Nyberg and Arthur Christensen, later teaching at Lund University (1941–1953) and Uppsala University (~1953–1974).
Stuart McFarlane is a scholar in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who held posts at Lancaster University, attested in 1991 and 2001 in the Department of Religious Studies.
Stuart Ray Sarbacker works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2001 under the supervision of David M. Knipe.

Su Bai was a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. After studying at Peking University (~1940–1948), he had a long career there, serving as Professor and becoming Professor Emeritus in the Archaeology Department (~1988–2018).

Subhadradis Diskul was a specialist in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the École du Louvre (~1948–1953). He served as President of the Siam Society (~1987–1990) and Chairman of The Jim Thompson Foundation.

Subhash Kak is an Indologist and historian who studied at NIT Srinagar and IIT Delhi. He held positions at Imperial College London (~1975–1976), Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Louisiana State University (attested 2005–2008).

Sudhir Kakar was a scholar of religious studies and other fields who studied at St. Edward's School, Shimla. He held posts at Harvard (~1971–1972), IIM Ahmedabad (~1972–1977), and IIT Delhi (~1977–1982).

Sue Hamilton works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned her D.Phil at the University of Oxford, studying under Richard Gombrich and Alexis Sanderson, and held an attested post at King's College London (2001–2003).
Suk Fun Ng specializes in Buddhist studies and completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) supervised by Jing Yin and Y. Karunadasa, having also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

Sukumar Sen was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. After studying at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1930), he held a post there (~1930–1964) and served as Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (~1954–1964).

Sukumari Bhattacharji was an Indologist who studied at the University of Calcutta and Jadavpur University. She held teaching positions at Lady Brabourne College (1945) and Jadavpur University (1957–1986).

Sulak Sivaraksa is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of Wales, Lampeter (~1954–1957). He served as editor for the Social Science Association of Thailand (~1963–1969) and with the Siam Society (attested 1992).

Sumanapala Galmangoda is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Indology. His career includes serving as director of the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (attested 2007) and Senior Professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 2012).

Sumathi Ramaswamy is an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Delhi, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and the University of Pennsylvania. She held academic posts at the University of Pennsylvania (~1993–2000) and the University of Michigan (~2000–2007).

Sumi Lee works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned an MA at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under Alexander L. Mayer and a PhD from the University of California, Los Angeles, supervised by Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Sumitra Mangesh Katre was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD at the University of London. He held posts at Sir Parashurambhau College, Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (1942–1971), and the University of Texas at Austin (~1971–1976).

Sun-Ah Choi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Juhyung Rhi and teachers Richard Neer, Robert S. Nelson, Jaś Elsner, and Aden Kumler.
